title: Opposition to amalgamation and working mostly in white clubs
summary: Some older members opposed merging, and she says she always worked in white establishments rather than black spots.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: Of course they had some opposition, from what they tell me. In fact I think some of the older members that are still around, they naturally did not see the advantage, you know. They were so used to going down to the old union. But the wonderful force behind the whole thing really won over, and it became a very marvelous thing for everybody. It was advantageous to everybody concerned, really; particularly to the black musicians, because they -- I don't think at the time that they were in a position to really remodel the old building or put money into it, and at that time it was just breaking, getting to the point where the black musicians were being accepted. There were some spots around town, they tell me, that really were not interested in employing black musicians. And I think just about this time, that this was all, you know, coming to pass. This was sort of behind us all, because fortunately, I always worked in the white establishments. I didn't have that problem, and I'm glad. I'm awfully glad of that. But I didn't have any problem. I worked, really I worked more in the white spots than I did in the black spots. I didn't work that many black spots.
